properties.name: io.revealbi.sbom.platform-resolution
properties.value: Explicit target engine selected; host-activated engine dependency replaced for cross-platform resolution.

properties.name: io.revealbi.sbom.inventory-scope
properties.value: Published Maven compile/runtime dependencies resolved at generation time, plus the engine embedded .deps.json. Provided servlet API and host operating-system libraries are excluded. Jackson uses the released POM range [2.13,3.0).

properties.name: reveal:vex:assessment-scope
properties.value: Reveal 2.3.2 published NuGet packages evaluated on .NET 8, Windows/Linux x64 Java and Node server distributions, and the browser npm runtime dependency manifest. Custom host integrations, host OS libraries, separately downloaded Chromium and prebundled browser subcomponents are outside scan coverage.

properties.name: reveal:vex:assessment-method
properties.value: Resolved published package graphs and inspected released embedded engine manifests. OSV-Scanner matched inventoried packages against complete local NuGet/npm/Maven databases with network access and transitive resolution disabled. Decisions use advisory prerequisites, released bytecode/decompilation, and runtime asset/reference inspection; unresolved configuration or call-path exposure remains in_triage.

components.name: json
components.description: JSON is a light-weight, language independent, data interchange format. See http://www.JSON.org/ The files in this package implement JSON encoders/decoders in Java. It also includes the capability to convert between JSON and XML, HTTP headers, Cookies, and CDL. This is a reference implementation. There are a large number of JSON packages in Java. Perhaps someday the Java community will standardize on one. Until then, choose carefully.

vulnerabilities.description: Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-70162 - .NET Denial of Service Vulnerability
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Upgrade System.Security.Cryptography.Pkcs to 8.0.2 or a supported patched version and repackage the self-contained engines.

analysis.detail: The affected API is EnvelopedCms.Decode on Windows. Static reference inspection of the released engine assemblies and selected NuGet runtime assemblies found no EnvelopedCms caller outside the Pkcs implementation and the System.Security type-forwarding facade. The Reports implementation uses SignedCms.ComputeSignature/Encode for output signing. No Reveal integration path to EnvelopedCms.Decode was identified. Custom host code that decodes CMS envelopes is outside this assessment.

vulnerabilities.description: Jetty has HTTP Request Smuggling via Chunked Extension Quoted-String Parsing

analysis.detail: The released CallbackServer constructs a direct HTTP/1.1 ServerConnector bound to 127.0.0.1. It has no reverse proxy/second HTTP parser in front of the callback endpoint, so the parser differential needed for the described smuggling scenario is absent. The handler also verifies the per-instance RevealBI-Auth token.

vulnerabilities.description: MySqlConnector: Account password disclosed to a man-in-the-middle in zero-configuration TLS mode (clear-text password sent before certificate is verified)
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Upgrade MySqlConnector to 2.6.1 or later; custom providers using VerifyCA/VerifyFull must configure SslCa until patched.

analysis.detail: The advisory requires VerifyCA or VerifyFull without SslCa. Decompiled released MySqlClient.GetConnectionString creates a MySqlConnectionStringBuilder and never sets SslMode or imports an arbitrary connection string; the released MariaDBProvider inherits MySqlProvider. MySqlConnector 2.3.5 declares Preferred as the SslMode default, and the four engine connector assemblies contain no set_SslMode reference. The advisory explicitly excludes Preferred/Required. Reassess any custom provider that enables VerifyCA/VerifyFull without SslCa; this decision does not assert that Preferred authenticates the server.

vulnerabilities.description: Apache Log4net: Silent log event loss in XmlLayout and XmlLayoutSchemaLog4J due to unescaped XML 1.0 forbidden characters

analysis.detail: The package is introduced by Snowflake.Data. Static reference inspection of the selected runtime and released engines found no XmlLayout or XmlLayoutSchemaLog4J use outside logging implementation assemblies. Reveal ships no configuration enabling those log4net layouts. This decision covers the supplied integration; a host that configures either XML layout must reassess and upgrade to log4net 3.3.0 or later.

vulnerabilities.description: Denial of service in ASP.NET Core

analysis.detail: The System.Private.Uri 4.3.0 entry is dependency-graph metadata, not the implementation used by the assessed .NET 8 runtime. Resolving the released Reveal.Sdk.Data 2.3.2 with CopyLocalLockFileAssemblies=true produced 143 copy-local references and none of the legacy Asn1, Http or RegularExpressions assemblies. The four distributed engine .deps.json files likewise have no runtime asset for the legacy Http/Private.Uri entries; the embedded .NET runtime packs are 8.0.34. This decision assumes a serviced .NET 8 host for the NuGet distribution and does not certify an older/custom host runtime.

vulnerabilities.description: SharpCompress has directory traversal via directory entries in WriteToDirectory (zip slip variant)

analysis.detail: MongoDB.Driver.Core 2.21.0 introduces this package for compression. Inspection of the selected NuGet runtime and all four engine assemblies found WriteToDirectory only inside SharpCompress itself, with no integration caller. The affected directory-extraction API is not invoked by the packaged Reveal/MongoDB compression path.

The System.Net.Http 4.3.0 entry is dependency-graph metadata, not the implementation used by the assessed .NET 8 runtime. Resolving the released Reveal.Sdk.Data 2.3.2 with CopyLocalLockFileAssemblies=true produced 143 copy-local references and none of the legacy Asn1, Http or RegularExpressions assemblies. The four distributed engine .deps.json files likewise have no runtime asset for the legacy Http/Private.Uri entries; the embedded .NET runtime packs are 8.0.34. This decision assumes a serviced .NET 8 host for the NuGet distribution and does not certify an older/custom host runtime.

Released CallbackServer bytecode creates ServerConnector(Server) with the default HTTP/1.1 connection factory. No HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 artifacts or connection factories are present in the Maven graph. The affected :authority/Host protocol combination is absent.

vulnerabilities.description: Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-84008 - .NET Denial of Service Vulnerability
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Upgrade System.Security.Cryptography.Pkcs to 8.0.2 or a supported patched version and repackage the self-contained engines.

analysis.detail: The affected API is SignedCms.CheckSignature. The vulnerable package is in the resolved graph and packaged engines. Static inspection found a SignedCms reference in the Windows Microsoft.Data.SqlClient runtime assembly as well as the Reports library. Reports uses ComputeSignature/Encode, but SQL Client attestation/signature-verification reachability has not been excluded for all supported connection configurations. No not_affected claim is made; confirm whether attacker-controlled CMS/X.509 data can reach CheckSignature or update the package.

vulnerabilities.description: Eclipse Jetty: Cross-Request Leakage for trailers on HTTP/1.1 keep-alive connections

analysis.detail: Inspection of every class in the released reveal-sdk-core and reveal-sdk-servlet JARs found no getTrailers reference. The callback handler does not consume HTTP trailers, so stale trailer fields cannot affect a Reveal callback decision.

vulnerabilities.description: JSON-java: JSONTokener Has Unbounded Numeric String Resource-Exhaustion DoS

analysis.detail: The published POM declares org.json, but inspection of every class in the released reveal-sdk-core and reveal-sdk-servlet JARs found no org/json, org.json or JSONTokener reference. Reveal uses Jackson for JSON parsing. No released integration caller reaches the affected JSON-java numeric-token parser.

vulnerabilities.description: Snappier has an infinite loop during SnappyStream decompression with malformed framed input

analysis.detail: Decompiled MongoDB.Driver.Core 2.21.0 SnappyCompressor calls Snappy.GetUncompressedLength and Snappy.Decompress block APIs. Static reference inspection found SnappyStream only inside Snappier itself. The affected framed-stream decompression path is not used.

Neither released Java SDK JAR references SecurityHandler.PathMapped, and the callback server installs a direct handler with token authentication instead of a path-mapped security handler. The affected configuration is absent.

vulnerabilities.description: org.eclipse.jetty:jetty-http has different parsing of invalid URIs

analysis.detail: The released Java integration uses the callback URI for endpoint/query routing and fixed local engine destinations; it does not enforce a host allowlist/denylist using Jetty parsing of an attacker-selected authority. No integration security decision depending on the described URI-parser differential was identified.
